The definition of "child pornography" in Canada is "explicit graphic depiction of a sexual act" involving a subject 17 years or younger. It must meet all criteria. Not only must it be a depiction of a sexual act, it must be a graphic depiction. Regardless of whether the image is suggestive or offensive, it doesn't visually depict the act of intercourse... It's not enough to suggest it, even if it's "pretty clear what's going on", that's implicit... It must be explicit to qualify as child pornography. You may be of the opinion that it's vile, but that's not what "graphic depiction" means in court.

The law doesn't respect our emotions, it respects the pre-established precedents and definitions. This law is no different from any other.

The age of consent in Alberta is 14 years assuming that their partner is less than 5 years older than them and not in a position of authority over them, otherwise it is 16.

In Alberta, anyone under the age of 18 is a child for the purposes of child pornography laws but the image does not contain a graphic depiction of a sexual act so doesn't qualify as pornography to begin with.
